papers.title_in_file: Does Data Complexity Predict Quantum Advantage? A framework, a pre-specified test, and an attribution of the measured edge
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv:2509.16410v2 (7 Oct 2026), a revision of the paper the record names ('Data complexity: a threshold between classical and quantum machine learning', v1). The four stored assertions are all from the v2 abstract and conclusion and are found in this file.

papers.what_it_is: A 69-page preprint that tests, under a pre-specified falsification battery over 8,100 simulated 8-qubit cells on 27 datasets, whether a data-complexity vector predicts the budget-matched quantum-classical edge, finds that it does not, and attributes the edge to the classical baseline, classical preprocessing and a near-chance quantum model.

assertions.value: The authors state that the validation suite exercised the topological component with a configuration (maximum dimension 1 and H0 explicitly zeroed) different from the deployed one, so the validated configuration was never the deployed one, and conclude that validating an estimator is not the same as validating the estimator as called.

The validated configuration was never the deployed one.
validating an estimator is not the same as validating the estimator as called, and only the latter licenses a null result.

assertions.value: The authors specify the corrected topological estimator: the backend is ripser with untruncated Rips persistence, H0 is excluded so only dimensions of at least 1 count, every bar is divided by the point cloud's diameter, and point clouds are subsampled to 250 points with a fixed seed.
quotes: H0 is excluded; only dimensions ≥ 1 count. Every bar is divided by the point cloud’s diameter, making the measure scale-invariant. Point clouds are subsampled to 250 points with a fixed seed.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the corrected estimator.
